title: To-do batch: Ollama system and UI errors

sections.title: Two items that overlap with what exists
sections.intro: Parallel work starts now, and the schedule system gets a design (types for your approval) first. These two items overlap with what's already built, so I'd like to know what you mean before an agent starts.

questions.question: The hub already has a built-in Ollama provider an admin configures (Models page; `execution/providers.ts`, `@aeye/ollama`). What should the Ollama system be?
questions.why: Two ways to reach the same Ollama would confuse admins; the answer decides whether the built-in goes away.

options.label: A system that replaces the built-in
options.description: An `ollama` system (installed, many instances: one per Ollama server) offers an aeye provider through the 'Providers from systems' mechanism: its config is the server URL, its model list is read live from the server, and admins (or people, per your wording) pick which models are offered. The hub's built-in Ollama provider type is removed and existing configs migrate to a system instance.

options.label: A system alongside the built-in
options.description: Add the system; keep the built-in provider type for hubs that don't install it.

options.label: Just a better model picker
options.description: No new system: improve the built-in so the person can pick from the Ollama server's live model list.

questions.question: "…the user can select models from": who picks which Ollama models are used?

options.label: An admin offers, a person picks per chat
options.description: An admin chooses which of the server's models are offered (with limits like num_ctx); people pick among them in a chat's model picker, as with other providers.

options.label: Anyone picks any model the server has
options.description: Every model the server lists is usable by everyone without an admin step.

questions.question: "Distinguishing to ui llm errors vs fn errors": which part is still mixed for you? (Model arg mistakes already show calmly as "Thinking harder · no bearing on the result", a40c00f.)

options.label: Model-call failures look like fn failures
options.description: When the model call itself fails (provider error, 429, timeout, out of credits, context too long), the chat shows it like a fn failure. Make it its own look: "the model couldn't answer" with the provider's reason and what to do (retry, another model), separate from a fn that failed.

options.label: Whose fault, at a glance
options.description: Every failure in the run tree and details says which side failed: the model (bad call, couldn't answer) or the fn/system (it ran and failed, or its system was down).

options.label: Already covered by the arg-mistake change
options.description: I wrote this before seeing a40c00f; nothing more needed.
